title: Hilt Graphs, Constructor Injection, and Modules Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best demonstrates sound hilt graphs, constructor injection, and modules?
options: Convert a manual accounts graph to Hilt using constructor injection, one Binds binding, and one Provides binding, then diagnose a deliberately missing dependency.
Writing Provides methods for every owned class instead of using constructor injection and readable requirements.
Copy the largest sample architecture without measuring its fit
Hide dependencies behind global lookup to reduce constructor parameters
questions.answer: Convert a manual accounts graph to Hilt using constructor injection, one Binds binding, and one Provides binding, then diagnose a deliberately missing dependency.
questions.explanation: The sound choice names the protected contract and requires observable evidence rather than structural appearance.

questions.prompt: Adding more interfaces and Gradle modules always improves application architecture.
questions.explanation: Every boundary has cost and must protect a real responsibility, change seam, ownership rule, or measured build property.

questions.prompt: What evidence should accompany the hilt graphs, constructor injection, and modules decision?
questions.answer: A focused behavioural test, dependency graph rule, failure scenario, or measurement tied to the claimed benefit.
questions.explanation: Architecture claims become reviewable when a specific check can prove or disprove them.
